reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes an investment app using rapid, unusually easy wealth claims, including 2.5% interest and a plan to earn 100,000 rupees in three days. It instructs viewers to register, bind a bank account, pay 1,000 rupees through a gateway, submit a transaction reference, and then expect the deposited amount plus earnings to be withdrawable. The creator also directs viewers to Telegram and urges interested viewers to participate, making this an endorsed solicitation rather than a warning or neutral demonstration.

then you click on recharge now and your app redirects you to gateway
After 3 days you will get the total amount And you can withdrew all money

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present the projected earnings as a commitment that every viewer will receive them. He limits participation to those who can take it on and says the decision is the viewer's responsibility. He also questions whether the higher check-in amounts are realistic. Those qualifications matter when assessing the investment discussion: a calculation and a hoped-for return are not proof that the speaker is certifying an outcome for everyone.

citations.quote: I am not asking everyone, only people who can do it. Your own responsibility will decide it.

i know everyone won't be able to do this but whoever is interested, you can do this

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited 100,000-rupee line is a stated plan, not evidence that anyone attained it. The three-day withdrawal line describes what the speaker expects from the application; it does not establish that viewers received that payout. The opening also omits his explicit statement that participation is the viewer's responsibility. The recharge instructions show how the process works, but they do not erase those qualifications.

citations.quote: I have a plan to earn 100 thousand rupees in 3 days without paying any tax.
After 3 days you will get the total amount And you can withdrew all money
I am not asking everyone, only people who can do it. Your own responsibility will decide it.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A personal-responsibility caveat does not change what the speaker asks viewers to consider doing. He calculates earnings from a 1,000-rupee investment, walks through recharge, and tells viewers they will get their total amount after three days. His doubts about the larger check-in rewards concern a separate benefit; they do not qualify the investment return he presents.

opening.argument: Judge, much of this is an operational walkthrough. The speaker says he will explain the process one step at a time, then demonstrates registration, verification and the payment flow. The sampled calculator screen shows investment inputs and a calculated result, not a record of future payouts to viewers. Reading the video as an explanation of an interface accounts for its detailed instructions without treating every displayed projection as an independently verified promise.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening correctly identifies the registration and recharge steps, but those steps are also the subject of the demonstration. A calculator result is not proof of an actual return, and the cited withdrawal statement concerns what the application is presented as doing after three days. The opening does not show a viewer's completed withdrawal following this walkthrough.

citations.quote: After 3 days you will get the total amount And you can withdrew all money

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is precisely how the solicitation becomes actionable. The speaker tells viewers to sign up, bind a bank account, recharge 1,000 rupees and invest it, while presenting daily earnings and a three-day withdrawal. A demonstration can still promote the transaction it demonstrates; no completed viewer withdrawal is needed to establish that the video encourages participation.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation also spends time on familiar app promotions: a sign-up bonus, check-in rewards and an envelope amount. The speaker even cautions that the higher check-in figures may not be attainable. The supplied material shows an app payment flow, but it does not show a viewer losing a deposit, a withheld withdrawal or a required recruiting chain. The visible reward features therefore deserve weight; the record should not be treated as proof that the service fails to pay simply because the speaker also discusses investing.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats the payment and transaction-reference steps as decisive. They establish that the speaker demonstrates a paid transaction, but not that a deposited balance was lost or that a withdrawal request was refused. Its bank-verification point likewise shows requested information, not what happened to that information afterward. The bonus and check-in discussion is substantial context for why a viewer might understand this as an app-rewards promotion.
